maya: Heads up — saw a perf regression in p99 after the queue-policy tweak landed last night. Profiling shows more KV evictions and a drop in continuous batch sizes for mid-length prompts. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

linus: Looking now. Do you have the profiler dump or a short replay? Could be kernel handoff latency or entrance classifier sending too many reqs to the microbatch path.

maya: Pasted small excerpt from the trace (trimmed):
```
request_id=rc-42 decode_rate_bucket=mid prompt_len_bucket=mid-16-64 token_budget_target=64 continuous_batch_size=3 kernel_switches=4 kv_evictions=7
request_id=rc-43 decode_rate_bucket=mid prompt_len_bucket=mid-16-64 token_budget_target=64 continuous_batch_size=2 kernel_switches=5 kv_evictions=9
```
Numbers are per-second aggregates around the spike.

dana: I replayed similar traffic on staging for ~10 minutes, saw kv_evictions/sec spike at 01:23 UTC when the new queue gating threshold was applied. Kernel selection logs also show a ~2x increase in `kernel_switches` for requests classified as mid.

sree: Probable cause: entrance classifier's decode-rate estimate is noisy in first few tokens, so it flips between microbatch and continuous-batch routes and triggers KV prefetch/evict churn. Quick mitigation: smooth decode_rate estimate with an EWMA over first N tokens or bias classifier toward continuous-batch for mid bucket.

harper: We also saw that `batcher.entrance.max_slices` config is 4 currently. That parameter allows early slice-off and can prevent larger continuous batches from forming. Lowering to 2 might increase batch coalescing but could slightly raise tail latency for tiny prompts.

maya: Can repro locally w/ replay: `./tools/replay --trace 2026-03-16 --bucket mid --duration 10m --profile` — I dumped the profiler into `out/profile-3265432100.pb`.

linus: Quick actionable plan: 1) add EWMA smoothing (alpha=0.4) for decode_rate estimate on entrance classifier, 2) raise mid-bucket token_budget_target from 64 -> 80 to give more headroom for continuous batches, 3) canary the config on a small pool. Also add `kernel_switch_rate` metric to the dashboard. If kernel_switch_rate drops, we reduced churn.

dana: I pushed a tiny PR that clamps decode_rate_estimate for first 8 tokens: `estimate = min(estimate, ewma(estimate, history, 0.4))` — nothing fancy, just damping. PR: https://git.redwood/repo/eng-runtime/pulls/892 (runbook attached).

maya: deploy-bot, canary the change to canary pool please?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started: eng-runtime/canary/3265432100 — classifier+config (mid_token_budget=80, decode_rate_smoothing=0.4)

harper: Nice. Also schedule a short-run A/B with lowering `batcher.entrance.max_slices` from 4 -> 2 for the mid bucket, see trade-off. I'll add a dashboard tile for `continuous_batch_size.p50/p95/p99` per bucket.

maya: Canary results (10m window): p99 latency improved from 210ms -> 185ms, median continuous batch size increased from 6 -> 9, kv_evictions decreased ~18%, kernel_switch_rate down ~36%. No measurable cost increase on token usage. Rolling to 10% traffic. :tada:

sree: Great news. Follow-ups: should smoothing be per-model? Some of our long-form models need longer windows. Also consider adding `prefix_entropy` as a classifier feature — low entropy prefixes are more likely to have short decodes.

dana: Filed follow-up ticket: RUNTIME-PLAT-1182 "Per-model entrance smoothing + prefix_entropy feature" with acceptance criteria and repro artifacts.

harper: And another to tune `entrance.min_hold_ms` for microbatch fallback (current 2ms -> try 6ms) so we give slightly more time for batch coalescing.

maya: OK I'll shepherd the rollout and keep the dashboard updated. Thanks y'all. :thumbsup:
